subject.title: [Feature/RFC]: Add eval-backed option discovery to avoid premature convergence in route/strategy answers

question: Should OpenClaw make anti-premature-convergence option discovery a default behavior invariant for route, strategy, and choice recommendations across the default OpenClaw and Codex harness paths?
rationale: The evidence shows a credible quality gap and no existing contract, but accepting it changes default model behavior and may increase search/tool cost across harnesses, so automation cannot choose the product boundary safely.

options.title: Accept eval-first invariant
options.body: Approve a generic QA Lab scenario and runtime-pair scope first, then consider a narrow prompt/runtime contract only after the eval shape is accepted.

options.title: Make it opt-in
options.body: Close the default-behavior request and track a separate research or best-insight profile where deeper option discovery is explicitly requested.

options.title: Decline for now
options.body: Leave current default behavior unchanged until repeated reproducible incidents justify the added prompt/tool cost.

recommendation.title: Accept eval-first invariant
recommendation.body: Approve a generic QA Lab scenario and runtime-pair scope first, then consider a narrow prompt/runtime contract only after the eval shape is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans Codex app-server lifecycle, default agent behavior, and product-scope tradeoffs; Peter has central history in the app-server lifecycle and core prompt surfaces.
